## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
All measured N (4000–4M) exceed the L1d spill at N≈963, so the curve starts in L2-resident territory. At q=0.01, ns/p is essentially flat from N=4000 (8.814) through N=262000 (8.164), with no knee at the L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 — cost even slightly improves, indicating overhead amortization dominates over cache effects. A gentle rise appears at N=1M (8.557) and N=4M (8.738), consistent with DRAM latency beginning to bite. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the N-curve: q=0.05 sits at ~8.7–9.3 ns/p and q=0.25 at ~11.2–11.9 ns/p, neither showing a spill knee. The N=4000 point is an outlier at higher death rates (11.588 at q=0.05, 14.058 at q=0.25), indicating per-particle overhead that amortizes away by N=16000.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.33 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — only 33% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. Bandwidth is flat across N at each death rate, indicating the algo is compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound: per-particle arithmetic (multiple fmul/fadd chains, RNG, scatter) dominates over data movement. Death rate transitions the floor downward: q=0.01 sustains ~8.0–8.3 GB/s, q=0.05 ~7.3–7.8 GB/s, and q=0.25 ~5.7–6.0 GB/s, with the drop attributable to branchy respawn and scatter cost rising with churn rather than to bandwidth saturation.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across the components of a single particle, not across particles. The update loop (0x100055324–0x100055384) uses `ldr q7` to load 4 floats, `ext.16b v17, v7, v16, #0xc` to rearrange, `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` for 4-wide component math, and `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` for the remaining pair. A gather appears: `ld1.s {v16}[1], [x11]` loads a single float into one vector lane from offset 0x14. The stride is `add x9, x9, #0x44` (68 bytes), matching bytes_per_particle. The scatter section (0x1000556e0+) uses `ldrb`/`strb` byte-granular stores with `csel` clamping — 19 strb and 12 ldrb instructions — which cannot stream and cap achievable bandwidth. The 26 vector-suffixed instructions are concentrated in the update loop; the scatter is entirely scalar.

## Verdict
Refuted — achieved bandwidth never exceeds 8.33 GB/s (33% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, N=262000, because component-wise vectorization operates on a stride-68 layout with a `ld1.s` gather and the scatter's byte-granular `strb` writes prevent streaming. Death rate further erodes it to 5.72 GB/s (23% of ceiling) at q=0.25. The hypothesis that autovec over per-particle components approaches the streaming ceiling does not hold in any regime.
